title: Find the K-Beauty of a Number
summary: Determine the k-beauty of an integer by counting its substrings of length k that divide the integer without remainder, allowing leading zeros and noting that 0 is not a divisor.
statement: Determine the k-beauty of an integer by counting its substrings of length k that divide the integer without remainder, allowing leading zeros and noting that 0 is not a divisor.
constraints: Inspect every contiguous length-k substring of the decimal representation, including ones with leading zeros.
Convert each substring to an integer; zero is not a divisor.
Count windows whose nonzero value divides num evenly.
hints: A fixed-size scan directly enumerates all candidate divisor substrings.
Parse each window; test nonzero before taking num modulo the value.
Loop index zero through len(text)-k inclusive and increment on value and num%value==0.
Every possible length-k substring appears at exactly one start index, so the count includes precisely the valid divisors.
